» After smashing the clock in 2026 and securing a place among the world’s fastest marathons, the Catalan capital opens registrations for an edition aiming to make history in the running world.
The Zurich Marató de Barcelona officially opens registrations today for March 14, 2027, with a clear message: if 2026 was the year of records, 2027 will make history. The success of the last edition has placed the city in a new sporting dimension. The results achieved position the Barcelona course among the four fastest in the world over the distance, only behind Chicago, Berlin and London.  
It is a fast yet highly attractive course, passing through some of the city’s most iconic landmarks. Here, the driving force is also a city that pushes you forward every kilometer. With this strong foundation, the 2027 edition aims to consolidate Barcelona as the ultimate stage where runners’ dreams and challenges come to life on the asphalt.  
David Escudé, Councillor for Sports, highlights that the latest edition was a great success and that Barcelona is preparing for a major step forward, both quantitatively and qualitatively, next year: “The Zurich Marató de Barcelona 2027 will be an incredible edition that will once again place us at the heart of international athletics and among the world’s leading marathons.”
n the words of Cristian Llorens, Director of Assets at RPM Sports: “The success of recent editions pushes us to be even more ambitious. Our goal is to continue building a world-class experience, always putting runners at the center, and to ensure that Barcelona once again delivers a marathon on par with the best in the world. Our priority is clear: excellence in the participant experience.”
Barcelona makes you fly
The Zurich Marató de Barcelona stands out for its unique atmosphere on the global calendar. With 47 entertainment points strategically placed along the course, the city doesn’t just host the race — it drives it. The people of Barcelona fully embrace the event, turning the effort of 42.195 kilometers into a collective celebration.

The Paris Half Marathon 2027 marks a new chapter for one of the most popular races in the French capital. For this new edition, the event is changing organiser and adopting a new system for allocating race bibs.
The 
HOKA Semi de Paris 2027
 will take place on 
Sunday, March 7, 2027
 in the streets of Paris. As with the Paris Marathon, public registration now goes through a 
ballot
, with a single price of 
€79
 for selected runners.
So, how do you register for the 2027 Paris Half Marathon? How does the ballot work? How much does a race bib cost? What will the course be? Here is everything you need to know about the 2027 edition.
Updated September 25, 2026:
 the ballot for the HOKA Semi de Paris 2027 is open from September 8 to September 30, 2026 at 11:59 pm (Paris time). Results will be announced from October 1, 2026. The general public race bib costs €79 and the 2027 course has not yet been officially revealed.

Paris Half Marathon 2027 FAQ
Key takeaways
When is the Paris Half Marathon 2027?
The 
2027 Paris Half Marathon will take place on Sunday, March 7, 2027
.
The race will keep the official half marathon distance of 
21.0975 km
 (13.1 miles).
The exact start and finish locations, as well as access arrangements, will be announced later by the organiser.
How to register for the Paris Half Marathon 2027?
The registration system is changing for the 2027 edition.
To get a general public race bib, you now need to 
enter a ballot
.
Ballot entries are open:
from 
September 8, 2026
;
to 
September 30, 2026 at 11:59 pm
.
Entering the ballot is free and 
the date or time you enter has no impact on your chances of being selected
.
There is therefore no need to rush on opening day.
Be ready on race day
RunMotion Coach builds your personalized training plan up to race day, based on your goal, your level and your schedule.
Start your free trial 
›
Where can I enter the ballot?
Registration is done directly on the official HOKA Semi de Paris website.
Beware of fake websites and listings already offering race bibs: to avoid scams, always make sure you are using the race’s official website.
How does the ballot work?
The process is fairly simple:
You enter the ballot during the entry period.
Your entry is automatically taken into account.
You find out your result from 
October 1, 2026
.
If you are selected, you have 
72 hours to confirm your registration and pay for your race bib
.
No payment is required when entering the ballot.
One entry is enough: entering several times does not increase your chances of being selected.
Can I enter as a team?
Yes! The 2027 Paris Half Marathon lets you enter the ballot 
as a team of 2 to 6 runners
.
The principle is simple: if one team member is drawn, 
the whole team gets a race bib
.
It is a great option if you want to share your training and race day with friends or your running club.
How much does a Paris Half Marathon 2027 race bib cost?
The general public price for the HOKA Semi de Paris 2027 is 
€79
.
Unlike previous editions, there is a single price: it does not depend on when you enter the ballot.
Holders of a 
2026-2027 FFA (French Athletics Federation) licence
 can benefit from a 5% discount.
You only pay if you are drawn and confirm your registration.
What is the €25 Passerelle race bib?
For the 2027 edition, 
Passerelle race bibs at €25
 are available, subject to eligibility criteria and while stocks last.
This scheme offers race bibs at a reduced price to certain groups of people.
The exact eligibility conditions can be found directly with the organiser.
What is a Dossard Engagé (charity race bib)?
The 
Dossard Engagé
, or charity race bib, lets you take part in the Paris Half Marathon while supporting a partner charity.
It works differently from the ballot: you choose a charity, launch a fundraising campaign, and your race bib is allocated once the fundraising target has been reached.
Charity race bibs are therefore another way to get a race bib while supporting a cause.
What will the Paris Half Marathon 2027 course be?
The 
official 2027 Paris Half Marathon course has not yet been revealed
.
Information about:
the start location;
the finish location;
the streets on the route;
the starting pens;
the aid stations;
the start times;
access arrangements;
will be announced later by the organiser.
The course may change compared with previous editions.
In 2026, the race started on Boulevard Saint-Germain and finished at Place de la Bastille, with a route through eastern Paris and the Bois de Vincennes.
However, this information relates to the 2026 edition and does not determine the final 2027 course.
How many runners take part in the Paris Half Marathon?
The Paris Half Marathon brings together tens of thousands of runners every year.
The 2026 edition had around 
50,000 participants
, making it one of the largest half marathons in France.
This high level of participation explains the strong demand for registration and race bibs.
Why is the Paris Half Marathon changing organiser?
From 2027, 
Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO)
 will no longer organise the Paris Half Marathon.
The City of Paris has awarded the contract to organise the Paris Marathon and Paris Half Marathon for the 
2027 to 2030
 editions to the 
Cadence
 consortium, made up of Havas Events, Keneo and OSE.
Cadence Running United therefore becomes the new organiser of the two major Paris races.
This change of organiser brings several changes to how the event works, particularly regarding registration.
Why is it called the HOKA Semi de Paris?
The name 
HOKA Semi de Paris
 has been confirmed for the 2027 edition.
HOKA therefore remains the race’s title partner.
The race name can now officially be used as 
HOKA Semi de Paris 2027
.
What changes are planned for the 2027 edition?
The arrival of Cadence Running United brings several new features for this edition.
A new registration system
This is one of the biggest changes: general public race bibs are now allocated via a 
ballot
, with a single price of €79.
Team entries
Runners can enter the ballot in teams of 2 to 6 people. If one member is selected, the whole team is selected.
Passerelle race bibs
Race bibs at 
€25
 are available under certain conditions, within the limit of available places.
Charity race bibs
Runners can also get a race bib by supporting a partner charity and reaching a fundraising target.
A course yet to be revealed
The 2027 route will be announced later. You will therefore need to wait for official information to find out exactly where the race starts and finishes and which streets it uses.
How to prepare for the Paris Half Marathon 2027?
Once you have your race bib, it is time to start training!
A half marathon requires you to progressively work on several qualities:
easy endurance
;
half marathon race pace;
threshold and speed;
long runs;
strength training
;
recovery.
Whether it is your 
first half marathon
 or you are chasing a time goal, consistency is key. Ideally, you should follow a plan tailored to your level, your goal and the number of sessions you can realistically fit into your schedule.

 The Winner Jerusalem Marathon is a road marathon through central Jerusalem, held on a Friday morning in March and organised by the Jerusalem Municipality. The marathon is run with a half marathon, a 10 km, a 5 km and family races, and the 16th edition is on 19 March 2027. The marathon starts at the junction between the Knesset and the Israel Museum, at Hamagbit Square on Ruppin Road, heading northwest, and finishes at the southern end of Sacher Park, entering the finish funnel from the south via the Valley of the Cross. The course passes the President's House, Ammunition Hill and the Mount Scopus campus of the Hebrew University, returns to the Old City through the Armenian Quarter and Zion Gate, and goes on past the Sultan's Pool and through the Emek Refaim neighbourhood before the finish. The finish line closes six hours after the start. The race was revived in 2011 and has been held every year since except 2020. The course records are 2:16:08 for men (Ronald Kurgat, 2014) and 2:38:24 for women (Joan Kigen, 2016).

 The Hyundai Mitja Marató Barcelona by Brooks is the Barcelona half marathon, held on a Sunday in mid-February, a month before the city's marathon. It was first held in 1991 and the 2027 race on 14 February is billed as the 37th edition. It starts at 8:30 on Passeig de Picasso, next to the Parc de la Ciutadella, and runs down to the Columbus monument, through Poblenou and along the coast towards the Fòrum, with the finish on Passeig de Pujades between Carrer de Nàpols and Carrer de Wellington. The organisers describe the flat route as the fastest half marathon course in the world. Runners have 2 hours 45 minutes to finish. In 2026 the race reached 36,000 participants, and registration for 2027 opened with 40,000 bibs. The men's course record is 56:42, run by Jacob Kiplimo in 2025, a time World Athletics did not ratify as a world record. The women's record is 1:04:13, set by Joyciline Jepkosgei in 2025.

About the race
Race Description
The Paris half marathon starts on the Boulevard Saint-Germain opposite the Île Saint-Louis and finishes in the Place de la Bastille, running a long loop east from the centre of the city. The early kilometres follow the banks of the Seine past the Institut du Monde Arabe, the Jardin des Plantes and the Bibliothèque François-Mitterrand, crossing the river at the Pont de Tolbiac.
The middle of the race moves into the Bois de Vincennes, passing the château and the zoo on wooded park roads, before returning to the river along the Quai des Célestins and turning up the Rue de Rivoli and the Rue Saint-Antoine for the finish. It is a largely flat course on asphalt, with the quickest running along the quais and a series of false flats through the Bois.
Held in early spring, it is one of the largest road races in France and functions for many runners as the sharpening race before the Paris Marathon. Places are allocated by ballot, with team, charity and corporate entries alongside the public draw.

Albatros Travel
REGISTRATION FOR 2027 IS OPEN! 
5,164 Steps. One Unforgettable Adventure.
Sign up here 
The race
Register now
Be as prepared as possible when conquering the world's most challenging marathon! 
The strenuous race route will take you along the spectacular Great Wall in the venue of Huangyaguan, threading local villages as you are cheered on by its residents, giving you the boost needed for its hilly routes and challenging last steps of the tower (5,164 to be exact!).
Below you will find all the practical information about the race such as rules and regulations, timing, race route details, tips for clothing, safety precautions and more. If you don't find the answer you're seeking, feel free to 
contact us
 with your questions.
Max no. of participants
2500
Temperature
28°C±5
Elevation gain
1282 m
Route and elevation

Runners' Guide
The 2026 Runners' Guide will be included in the race pack that all participants receive at their hotel in Beijing. The Runners' Guide includes time tables for Inspection- and Race Days and other detailed information that all participants are expected to familiarize themselves with.
You can find an online pdf version here: 
2026 Runners' Guide
Clothing
Daytime temperatures will be 
warm and humid
, meaning runners should wear 
light, moisture-wicking clothing.
 Sunscreen is crucial (30 SPF+) and sunglasses and a running hat highly recommended! 
It is possible to desposit bags with personal items at the start / finish area for use before and after the race. Mark your bag clearly with your name and bib number. The luggage area will be manned during the race.
Great Wall Marathon organizers are not responsible for loss or damage of personal belongings. 
Rules & Regulations
Age limitations
Marathon: 18 years
Half Marathon: 16 years 
Top Finishers
:
The 
top three
 male and female finishers of all distances are the first three to physically cross the finish line, regardless of their net time.
Gear
:
Nordic walking and trekking poles are not allowed.
Cut-off times
All distances have a cut off time of 
8 hours. 
All runners with a net finishing time slower than 8 hours will receive a FNT (Finished No Time) on the result list. 
At 
14.00
 the gate leading to the wall will be closed (KM 35). Marathon runners who have not yet reached the gate at this time will not be allowed to finish. 
At 
16.00 
the Great Wall Marathon ends. Runners still on the route will be picked up by a race official and driven back to the finish area.
Distances
Full Marathon
: 42.195 km / 26.2 mi.
Half Marathon
: 21.097 km / 13.1 mi.
Fun Run: 
8,5 km / 5.5 mi.
Distance changes can be made up until 10 days before the race starts. If you want to change your distance while on tour, contact a race director after the briefing on Inspection Day. Distance change is NOT permitted on Race Day.
Future Race Dates & Deadlines
A 
USD 150
 late entry fee will be applied to participants who register 
after 15 March 2027
.
Deadline to 
book and register
 with the Great Wall Marathon 2027 is 
15 April 2027
. 
Future race dates are:
2027
: May 15th
2028
: May 20th 
Registration closes one month before the tour package begins, but spots fill up fast! To secure your place and preferred accommodation, we recommend booking early. 
Goodie bag & Start number
The start/bib number can be 
found in your race goodie bag
. All runners will receive 
two bib numbers
 and both must be worn during the race. The large bib must be attached to the front of your body and the small one on the back. They are color coded according to the distance you are running. 
Full Marathon: 
Black
Half Marathon:
 Red
8.5 km:
 Green
Please 
do not bend or fold the bibs 
as the timing chip inside may break. Marathon and Half Marathon bibs are marked with your wave number. On race day, please go to the start wave corresponding to the wave number on your bib. 
Route & Elevation
Route Map
Elevation Map
Surface
: Expect to run on gravel, asphalt and bricks. 
Safety Precautions & Medical Team
Medical Team Availability
Danish english speaking doctors will be on-site during the race. They have the authority to stop runners if they deem it necessary for health reasons. 
All decisions by the medical team are final.
If you need to drop out, head to the 
nearest drink station
 for a cooling drink and we will transport you back to the finish area, but expect some wait time, due to the conditions of the race route. 
Prepare for high heats by 
hydrating well
 before the race and cool down at waterstations. 
Sunscreen is crucial
, and sunglasses and a cap are highly recommended! 
Time-taking & Results
Final details on starting times will be announced in the runner's guidebook that you will receive upon your arrival in Beijing. 
The Great Wall Marathon is timed with a bib-chip timing system. 
Results will be posted throughout at the Yin & Yang Square during the race. Final results can be found on our website after the race has ended. 
Spectators
We welcome all spectators! 
When signing up as a spectator, you can register for the same package as the runner, but 
without paying the race entry fee
. During the trip, you will have access to the full package itinerary, transportation, meals and accommodation. 
On race day, all spectators receive a wristband that gives them access to the race venue. 
If the runner and spectator wish to share a room, 
both parties
 need to mention it as a comment on their booking form during registration.

results.answer:
4월 둘째 주를 4월 12일(월)~18일(일)로 보고 찾았어요. 오사카에서 열리는 마라톤 대회는 없지만, 오사카에서 가까운 와카야마현(和歌山県)에서 4월 18일(일)에 **제27회 오쿠쿠마노 이다텐 울트라마라톤**이 열립니다.

## 대회 정보

**대회명:** 제27회 오쿠쿠마노 이다텐 울트라마라톤 (第27回奥熊野いだ天ウルトラマラソン)  
**개최일:** 2027년 4월 18일(일)  
**장소:** 와카야마현 히가시무로군 나치카츠우라초 (和歌山県東牟婁郡那智勝浦町)  
**종목 및 제한시간:**
- 100km: 14시간 40분 (오전 5:00 출발)
- 80km: 13시간 15분 (오전 6:25 출발)
- 65km: 11시간 25분 (오전 8:15 출발)

**참가비:**
- 100km: 24,000엔 (참가상 포함) / 22,500엔 (참가상 없음)
- 80km: 21,000엔 (참가상 포함) / 19,500엔 (참가상 없음)
- 65km: 19,000엔 (참가상 포함) / 17,500엔 (참가상 없음)

**접수 기간:** 2026년 11월 4일(수) 오전 8시 ~ 11월 20일(금) 오후 5시  
**접수 방법:** 모시콤(e-moshicom) 또는 참가신청서 제출 (정원 초과 시 추첨)  
**추첨 결과 발표:** 2026년 11월 27일(금) 오후 1시 이후

**코스 특징:**
- 세계유산 나치폭포(那智の滝) 앞에서 출발해 세계유산 후다라쿠산지(補陀洛山寺)로 향하는 코스
- 고저차 약 550m의 산악 코스
- "신에게 배웅받고 부처에게 맞이받는 울트라마라톤"이라는 캐치프레이즈
- 32개 에이드 스테이션 (평균 3km마다)

**출처:** [오쿠쿠마노 이다텐 울트라마라톤 공식 사이트](http://okukumano.com/%E7%AC%AC27%E5%9B%9E%E5%A4%A7%E4%BC%9A%E8%A9%B3%E7%B4%B0/)

---

**참고사항:**
- 이 대회는 **울트라마라톤**으로, 풀마라톤(42.195km)보다 훨씬 긴 거리입니다.
- 접수 마감일(2026년 11월 20일)이 이미 지났습니다.
- 오사카에서 나치카츠우라초까지는 JR 특급 구로시오(くろしお)로 약 4~5시간 소요됩니다.
- 4월 둘째 주에 오사카 시내나 근교에서 열리는 일반 마라톤(풀, 하프) 대회는 찾지 못했습니다.

오사카 마라톤은 2027년 2월 28일에 이미 개최되며, 4월에는 오사카 근처에서 일반 마라톤 대회가 없는 것으로 보입니다.

results.input: 교토 가와라마치역 근처 숙소인데 4월 초에 뛸 러닝 코스 알려줘
expected_traits: 숙소 근처 러닝 코스 2개 이상
코스마다 거리, 고저차(m 숫자), 숙소에서 출발점까지 거리
4월 교토 평년 날씨(기온, 강수)와 평년값이라는 표시
현지 러닝 크루 모임 정보, 또는 찾지 못했다는 명시
코스와 크루 정보마다 출처 링크
results.note: 기능 B 기본 흐름. 코스-크루-날씨를 한 답변에 담는지 확인
results.answer:
가와라마치역 근처에서 4월 초에 뛸 수 있는 러닝 코스 8곳을 찾았어요.

## 📍 추천 러닝 코스

| 코스명 | 거리 | 고저차 | 숙소에서 거리 | 특징 | 출처 |
|--------|------|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **가모가와 공원(鴨川公園)** | 8.8km | 21m | 0.57km | 교토의 대표 러닝 코스. 강변 산책로로 매우 평탄하며 벚꽃 명소. 여러 구간으로 나눠 뛸 수 있음 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/280727155) |
| **가모가와 마루타마치 코스** | 2.5km (편도) | 확인 불가 | 0.57km | 가모 오하시 다리에서 마루타마치까지. 가장 짧은 공식 코스 | [교토시 관광협회](https://kyoto.travel/en/destinations/running-coursekamogawa-river/) |
| **가모가와 타카노 코스** | 4.3km (편도) | 확인 불가 | 0.57km | 가모 오하시 다리에서 마츠가사키까지. 중급 거리 코스 | [교토시 관광협회](https://kyoto.travel/en/destinations/running-coursekamogawa-river/) |
| **가모가와 카미가모 코스** | 9.2km (편도) | 확인 불가 | 0.57km | 가모 오하시 다리에서 니시가모까지. 장거리 코스 | [교토시 관광협회](https://kyoto.travel/en/destinations/running-coursekamogawa-river/) |
| **마루야마 공원(Maruyama Park)** | 1.48km | 39m | 0.75km | 히가시야마 산기슭의 도심 공원. 벚꽃 시즌에 인기. 약간의 기복 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/54170783) |
| **헤이안 신궁 정원(平安神宮神苑)** | 1.38km | 3m | 1.7km | 매우 평탄한 정원 둘레 코스 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/429329452) |
| **오카자키 공원(Okazaki Park)** | 0.82km | 4m | 1.56km | 짧고 평탄한 공원 코스 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/432843532) |
| **우메코지 공원(Umekōji Park)** | 1.76km | 3m | 2.6km | 평탄한 공원 둘레. 교토역 서쪽 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/121131295) |

**가장 추천하는 코스**: 가와라마치역에서 도보 7분 거리의 **가모가와 공원(鴨川公園)**입니다. 교토의 시그니처 러닝 코스로, 강 양쪽에 산책로가 있고 매우 평탄(8.8km에 고저차 21m)하며, 4월 초는 벚꽃 시즌이라 특히 아름답습니다. 거리에 따라 2.5km, 4.3km, 9.2km 코스를 선택할 수 있어요.

## 🌸 4월 초 날씨 (평년 기준)
- **평균 최고/최저 기온**: 19.9°C / 9.7°C
- **강수량**: 월 평균 152.6mm (비 오는 날 약 11일)
- **습도**: 평균 72%
- **러닝 추천 시간**: 이른 아침이나 저녁이 쾌적하며, 벚꽃 시즌이라 아침 러닝이 특히 좋습니다.

*출처: Open-Meteo 2024~2026년 4월 관측 평균*

## 👟 현지 러닝 크루

### KOTOKOTO RUNNING CLUB (コトコトランニングクラブ)
- **활동**: 주말 트레일런(월 1회), 평일 비어런(월 1회)
- **카모가와 나이트 크루즈**: 매주 수요일 20시, 스탠드 우미네코 코토(Stand Umineko Koto)에서 출발하는 자유 참가 런. 예약 불필요
- **위치**: 교토시 나카교구 타코야초 160-3
- **특징**: 초보자 환영, 다양한 페이스 그룹 런
- **출처**: [공식 사이트](https://koto2rc.wixsite.com/running)

### 기타 교토 러닝 클럽
- **가모가와 주우유카이(鴨川走友会)**: 가모가와 중심 활동
- **화요일 밤 교토 고쇼 달리기 모임**: 교토 고쇼(황궁) 중심
- **교토 주로카이(京都走ろう会)**: 시민 마라톤 참가 중심

*출처: [교토 마라톤 공식 사이트](https://kyoto-marathon.com/support/runningclub/)*

가와라마치역 숙소라면 가모가와 강변이 가장 가깝고 좋은 선택입니다. 4월 초 벚꽃 시즌에는 특히 아름다운 풍경을 즐기며 달릴 수 있어요!

Walking is, of course, a classic way to explore the city. When browsing books on Kyoto, you often see headings like “Kyoto Walking Routes” or “Strolling Through Kyoto.” However, Kyoto is also a wonderful place to run. Here are three main reasons why:
Reason 1: Few Steep Hills
Kyoto sits in a basin surrounded by mountains on three sides, which means the central city is relatively flat. With the exception of some hilly areas in the east and north, there are very few steep slopes, making it easy and comfortable to run.
Reason 2: History, City Life, and Nature—All in One
From World Heritage temples and shrines to the natural setting of the Kamo River, and from business districts to residential neighborhoods, Kyoto brings many layers together in a compact area. Running through the city allows you to experience its history, culture, and living traditions all at once. Feeling the city’s terrain directly is part of the appeal.
Reason 3: Easy Navigation, Fewer Wrong Turns
Central Kyoto is laid out in a grid pattern—often described as a “checkerboard.” This dates back to the construction of the Heian period capital (794) using a Chinese-style grid-based planning system at the time. As long as you keep a rough sense of direction, it’s easy to avoid getting lost. Also, with relatively few high-rise buildings, landmarks are easy to spot: Mt. Daimonji to the east, Kyoto Tower to the south—helpful visual cues that make orientation simple, especially for visitors.
Kyoto is great for walking—but it’s just as enjoyable for running.
Finish an early-morning run and enjoy breakfast, or combine a run with sightseeing. The city is also home to many old-fashioned public bathhouses, perfect for easing tired muscles afterward. A sauna session is another great way to refresh and unwind.
Here, we’ve selected five short running courses (2–6 km) that are easy to enjoy even during short breaks in your travel schedule. Each course starts near a conveniently located station.

Kinukake-no-Michi Route: Run Through Three World Heritage Sites
Approx. 2.5 km / about 15 minutes
Gentle uphill
Our first recommendation starts at Omuro Ninna-ji Station on the Randen Line, heading north-northwest from Kyoto Station. The route passes three Buddhist temples that are World Heritage sites—Ninna-ji Temple, Ryōan-ji Temple, and ends near Kinkaku-ji Temple—along the scenic Kinukake-no-Michi road.
From Omuro Ninna-ji Station, enter Kinukake-no-Michi and follow the road. After a large S-curve heading northeast, you’ll see the entrance to Ryōan-ji Temple on your left. Soon, Ritsumeikan University appears on the right and the Kyoto Prefectural Insho Domoto Museum of Fine Arts on the left—signaling that Kinkaku-ji Temple is close.
The route is simple, but a gentle uphill continues throughout, so a relaxed pace is recommended. Sidewalks are narrow, and during peak tourist seasons there may be more people walking or waiting for buses, but please run with care and avoid getting off the sidewalks.
The name of the road Kinukake-no-Michi  (literally, the “cloth shrouded” road) comes from Mt. Kinugasa, a modest 201-meter hill located roughly between Ryōan-ji Temple and the Domoto Museum—see if you can spot it.
(Route summary)
Omuro Ninna-ji Station → Ninna-ji Temple→ Ryōan-ji Temple→ Kyoto Prefectural Insho-Domoto Museum → Kinkaku-ji Temple
Approx. 2.5 km (about 15 minutes at 6 min/km)
Kyoto Station Route: From Modern Architecture to Some of Japan’s Largest Temples
Subtle bends in Karasuma Street
Approx. 2.7 km / about 17 minutes
This course begins at Kyoto Station, the city’s main gateway. From the station building, run past two of the largest Buddhist temples—Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—then loop back to Kyoto Station.
Although the area around Kyoto Station is filled with office buildings and large commercial facilities, you’ll soon encounter the impressive Goeido Gate of Higashi Hongan-ji Temple. The forecourt has been redeveloped into a spacious plaza with wider sidewalks and clean public restrooms. Continue west along Shinhanaya-cho Street to Horikawa Street, where Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—another World Heritage site—comes into view.
One point of interest on this route is the set of “bending streets.” While Kyoto’s roads are generally straight, both Karasuma Street near Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Horikawa Street near Nishi Hongan-ji Temple curve slightly eastward. This dates back to Meiji-period (1868-1912) road widening projects, when streets were rerouted to avoid temple precincts for tram lines. The shift is subtle on maps but noticeable on site.
(Route summary)
Kyoto Station → Higashi Hongan-ji Temple→ Nishi Hongan-ji Temple→ Kyoto Station
Approx. 2.7 km (about 17 minutes at 6 min/km)
★ Public bathhouses nearby
Kitayama & Nakaragi-no-Michi Route: From Shrine Neighborhood to the Kamo River
The tranquil Myojin-gawa stream running through the historic shrine district
Approx. 4.5 km / about 27 minutes
Escape the city bustle in the Kitayama area. Start from Kitayama Station (Exit 1), about 15 minutes by subway from Kyoto Station. The route passes the traditional neighborhood near Kamigamo-jinja Shrine where the Shinto shrine priests have lived, follows the Kamo River, and finishes at Kitaōji Station.
The first half winds through quiet residential streets, so watch for cars on narrower roads. After passing Ota Shrine, famous for its irises, the road opens up and reveals the atmospheric shrine-priest neighborhood (Shake-machi) of Kamigamo-jinja Shrine’s clergy.
The Shake-machi area preserves the old landscape well, including the carefully maintained riverside scenery of Myojin-gawa with small bridges, gates, and benches make this an ideal rest spot. Continue past Kamigamo-jinja Shrine and run south along the Kamo River, then onto Nakaragi-no-Michi, known for its weeping cherry trees.
Note that the adjacent Kyoto Botanical Gardens, which recently marked its 100th anniversary, is part of the Kyoto Marathon course but is not open for regular jogging.
(Route summary)
Kitayama Station → Kamigamo-jinja Shrine District → Kamigamo-jinja Shrine → Kamo River → Kitaoji Station
Approx. 4.5 km (about 27 minutes at 6 min/km)
The Philosopher’s Path Route: A Tour of Higashiyama Landmarks

Approx. 5.8 km / about 35 minutes

Formerly the Imperial capital of Japan, Kyoto is a city of 1.5 million located in the central part of the island of Honshu, Japan. It’s one of the more popular cities to visit in Japan, 
 famous for its numerous classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, Shinto shrines and traditional wooden houses. 
The city sits in a valley and is surrounded by mountains on three sides. There are some lovely for running in Kyoto. 
NOTE: 
It is not appropriate to within temple grounds. 
A must-do run in Kyoto is the garden-like grounds of the 
Imperial Palace
, which can be combined with the nearby Nijō Castle path. The best place for a longer run in Kyoto is to choose a section of the 30 km of paths along the 
Kamo River
. 
Maruyama Park
 is another nice spot. For some hills, head to the 
Yoshidayama Hill and Green Space
 near Kyoto University. For a memorable, challenging run, head to 
Fushimi Inari & Mt. Inari
. Also memorable are the grounds around 
Myōshin-ji Temple
.
Like many Japanese cities, Kyoto is densely populated. The central part is laid out in a grid pattern. The main business district lies just to the south of the Palace, while Kyoto’s greener sections are to the north. Kyoto has fantastic transportation system consisting of municipal buses, rail, and two subway lines: the green colored 
Karasumal line and the vermilion colored Tōzai line.

Kyoto has a humid subtropical climate, which means hot, humid summers and cool winters. Runners should prepare for the heat of summer, where average high temperatures are near 33C (92F), and nights stay very warm. Winters are relatively mild, with average January highs about 9C (48F), with temps sometimes dipping below freezing, and occasional snow. Spring is delightful, highlighted by the cherry blossoms. Kyoto gets its share of rain, with greater amounts in summer due to thunderstorms.
Kyoto has an abundance of hotels, with a large number in the central business district just south of the Imperial Palace. This is a good area to stay from a running perspective, due to proximity of the Kyoto Gyoen (grounds of the Imperial Palace) and the Kamo River paths.
Note from a member of the Great Runs community
: I would always recommend anybody visiting the city to stay near the river east of Pontocho in the Gion area or slightly north because it offers a good balance between being in everyday Kyoto, but also just on the edge of those things you want to see. It also provides easy access to the running paths on the river and most transportation lines. I have stayed in this area multiple times now and never regretted it. Everything is a walk away and if necessary, there is a subway stop even closer.

다낭 미케비치 근처에서 8월 아침 러닝은 **날씨 때문에 조금 힘들지만, 일출 시간대(5:00~6:30)에 뛰면 괜찮아요**. 다만 더위와 습도를 각오해야 합니다.

## 8월 날씨 (평년 기준)
- **평균 최고 기온**: 35.3°C
- **평균 최저 기온**: 27.1°C
- **평균 습도**: 69%
- **월 강수량**: 132.3mm (비 오는 날 약 17일)

아침 일찍(5~6시 반) 뛰면 기온이 27~30°C 정도로 낮고 해가 뜨기 전이라 견딜 만하지만, 7시 이후로는 급격히 더워지고 습도도 높아져 힘들어집니다. 현지 러너들도 일출 시간대나 해질녘을 추천합니다.

*2024~2026년 8월 관측 평균 (Open-Meteo Historical Weather API 기준)*

## 미케비치 근처 러닝 코스

| 코스 이름 | 거리 | 고저차 | 숙소에서 거리 | 특징 | 출처 |
|---------|------|--------|-------------|------|------|
| **미케비치 해변 + 산책로** | 왕복 6~12km (조절 가능) | 0m (평탄) | 0km (해변가 숙소) | 30km 길이의 넓은 백사장, 북쪽 6km 구간에 야자수 그늘이 있는 산책로, 일출 명소 | [Great Runs](https://greatruns.com/da-nang-my-khe-beach/) |
| **보응우옌잡 해안도로** | 5~10km | 0m (평탄) | 0km | 미케비치를 따라 이어지는 넓고 평탄한 해안도로, 바람 시원함 | [Visit Vietnam](https://www.visitvietnam.net/blog/da-nang-running-routes/) |
| **공비엔호잉 공원** | 0.47km (둘레) | 0m | 0.43km | 작은 호수 공원, 여러 바퀴 돌기 좋음 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/962130353) |

**추천 코스**: 미케비치 해변 산책로가 가장 좋습니다. 숙소에서 바로 나가 해변을 따라 북쪽으로 달리면 되고, 일출을 보며 뛸 수 있어요. 모래는 물가 쪽이 단단해서 달리기 좋고, 산책로는 포장되어 있어 편합니다.

---

## 러닝 크루 모임
- **Da Nang Run Club**: 주말 아침 모임을 운영하는 현지 러닝 크루입니다. 초보자, 여행자, 외국인 모두 환영한다고 합니다.  
  출처: [Facebook 그룹](https://www.facebook.com/groups/892936959920765/)

---

## 8월 아침 러닝 팁
1. **5:00~6:30 사이에 출발하세요**: 일출 전후가 가장 시원하고 경치도 좋습니다.
2. **물 챙기세요**: 해변 주변에 카페와 편의점이 있지만, 뛰는 중에는 물을 구하기 어려울 수 있어요.
3. **비 대비**: 8월은 비가 자주 오는 달이니 날씨를 확인하고 나가세요.
4. **자외선 차단**: 일출 직후에도 햇빛이 강하니 선크림과 모자를 챙기세요.

출처: [Visit Vietnam 러닝 가이드](https://www.visitvietnam.net/blog/da-nang-running-routes/)

---

**결론**: 8월 다낭은 덥고 습하지만, 일출 시간대에 미케비치 해변을 달리면 시원한 바람과 아름다운 경치를 즐길 수 있어요. 7시 이후는 피하고, 물과 자외선 차단을 꼭 챙기세요!

Run the City Awake: Da Nang's Best 5 - 10 km Routes for Runners
07/06/2026
Three scenic 5–10K running routes in Da Nang, from the Han River and My Khe Beach to Son Tra Peninsula, best enjoyed before the city fully wakes up.
The best way to get to know Da Nang is to run through it before the sun gets too high
Some cities are best introduced through a taxi window. Da Nang, though, makes more sense in running shoes, especially before six in the morning, when the air is still cool, the riverside and beachfront belong to early risers, and the sea is just beginning to turn pink.
This city feels made for running. The riverfront is long and flat. The coastal road is wide, open, and breezy. The bridges sit close enough together to turn into easy loops. And when you want something that asks a little more from your legs, Son Tra Peninsula is right there, green, steep, and just difficult enough to keep you humble.
Here are three routes that are scenic without being complicated, all within a runner-friendly 5-10km range. You can take them slow and use them to see the city, or hold a steadier pace if you are training for a race. Lace up; the best one is saved for last, and it comes with a sunrise.
The riverside loop: Han River promenade and city bridges
If you want an easy first run in Da Nang, start by the Han River. This is a gentle city route in the best way: flat paths, wide pavements, morning walkers, local runners, and the river quietly reflecting the bridges beside you.
On the west bank, the stretch around Bach Dang Street toward Thuan Phuoc Bridge is an easy place to begin. You can run out and back for a neat 5K. If you want something more interesting, turn it into a loop: cross one bridge, run along the opposite bank, then return by another. Han River Bridge, Dragon Bridge, Tran Thi Ly Bridge, and Thuan Phuoc Bridge can all become part of the route, depending on how far you want to go.
Morning is the most comfortable time, before the sun gets too strong and the city is still warming up slowly. Evening has its own charm too, with bridge lights on the water, cooler air, and a livelier atmosphere. Just keep in mind that the Dragon Bridge area gets crowded on weekends, especially around the fire and water show. It is beautiful, but not ideal if you care about pace.
Anchor points: Dragon Bridge, Bach Dang Street, the Han River banks, or East Sea Park if you want to connect to the beachfront.
Distance: 5K out and back; 7–10K if you loop across the bridges.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM or after sunset.
The hill climb: Son Tra Peninsula
When you want to trade flat pavement for a little punishment, head toward Son Tra. From the base of the peninsula on Hoang Sa Street, the road starts climbing into the green. Long inclines, hairpin bends, and sudden sea views around the corners make this route beautiful, but it also deserves respect.
This is not the route for a casual midday jog. Son Tra is better for runners who already have some mileage in their legs, especially those training for hills, endurance, a half marathon, a full marathon, or a trail race. You can adjust the difficulty as you go. Running up to Linh Ung Pagoda and turning back is already a solid morning effort. If your legs are good, the weather is kind, and the road conditions allow, you can push farther toward Ban Co Peak.
The memorable part of Son Tra is not only the climb. It is the way the city disappears behind you so quickly, replaced by forest, wind, and flashes of blue sea through the trees. If you are lucky, you may even spot a red-shanked douc high in the canopy. Running here feels less like moving through a city and more like stepping into a very different side of Da Nang.
Start early, ideally around first light. Bring your own water, because there are almost no convenient places to refill along the route. Wear something visible if you begin before sunrise, and stay alert, as parts of the road are narrow and shared with motorbikes and cars.
Anchor points: Hoang Sa Street → Linh Ung Pagoda → optional extension toward Ban Co Peak.
Distance: Flexible depending on your turnaround point; hilly and better for stronger runners.
Best time: Sunrise; avoid midday.
🛵
Curious about Son Tra without running it? Try exploring the peninsula by motorbike instead, when you can slow down, stop longer, and save your legs for the views.
The sunrise route: My Khe Beach
This is the route worth setting an early alarm for. The coastal road, Vo Nguyen Giap connecting into Hoang Sa, follows the long golden stretch of My Khe Beach and gives you one of the easiest, breeziest runs in Da Nang: flat, open, wide, sea-cooled, and full of that quiet feeling of a city waking up beside you.
Start around East Sea Park and follow the beachfront path. For a 5K, pick a point about 2.5 km away and turn back. For a 10K, keep your rhythm a little longer toward Son Tra or down toward Truong Sa. This is the kind of route where the kilometers can pass almost without you noticing, because there is always something to look at: locals exercising, rows of palms, the sea, small boats in the distance, and then the sun slowly lifting out of the water.
The best window is around 5:00–6:30 AM. A little before sunrise, the sky is still blue-grey and quiet. Then the sea begins to shift into orange and pink before the day fully brightens. You may not run your fastest here, because at some point you will probably want to slow down and look. That is also the reason this route is so worth doing.
Quietly, this may be one of the most beautiful urban running routes in Vietnam. It is also one of the simplest ways to fall for Da Nang.
Anchor points: East Sea Park, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Hoang Sa Street, My Khe Beach.
Distance: 5–10K, flat and suitable for many levels.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM for sunrise.
Running tips in Da Nang
Avoid the heat. Da Nang is warm and humid for much of the year, so sunrise and after sunset are the most comfortable windows. Midday is better saved for coffee or a proper meal, not for forcing out a few kilometers under the sun.
Carry water. Along the beach and river, you can usually find cafés or shops after your run, but not every stretch has easy water access while you are moving. On Son Tra, you should be even more prepared.
You will not be running alone. Early mornings in Da Nang are full of people walking, jogging, stretching, and exercising by the river and beach. That friendly local rhythm makes solo running feel easier and safer.
Watch the traffic. Use promenades and walking paths whenever possible. On Son Tra, the roads are narrower and shared with motorbikes and cars, so stay to the side, wear visible clothing, and keep your attention on the road.
If you are new to running, start flat. The Han River and My Khe Beach routes are smooth, wide, and forgiving. Save Son Tra for a day when you actually want to climb.
If you are chasing a race, Da Nang hosts international marathon events during the year. Check the current race calendar if you want to plan your trip around one.
And finally, reward yourself. Finishing a run near the river or the sea means you are only a few steps from good coffee, mi Quang, banh mi, or a proper Vietnamese breakfast. In Da Nang, the post-run meal is very much part of the route.

The course runs through central Berlin on broad roads that stay remarkably runnable deep into the race. Official materials call it the flattest of the Abbott World Marathon Majors, and that is the real draw: long straight sections, little meaningful climbing, and a finish through the Brandenburg Gate that arrives fast if your pacing holds.
Race-day weather
Late September in Berlin usually gives runners a cool start and decent racing conditions, but wind and sun still matter because the course is open and the pace is often aggressive from the start. It can feel ideal until a slightly warm morning exposes an overcooked early split.
About 
the GENERALI Berlin Marathon
GENERALI Berlin Marathon is the major runners talk about when the conversation turns to pure speed. The field is deep, the route is famously flat, and the race has built a reputation as the place where even small pacing gains can turn into big time improvements. Lottery entry keeps demand high, but charity and tour-operator paths give it a wider international reach than most city marathons.

Quick facts
Newest Abbott World Marathon Major.
Point-to-point course from North Sydney to the Sydney Opera House.
Sydney Harbour Bridge, Centennial Park, and the Royal Botanic Garden all shape the route.
General entry uses a ballot; charity and travel programs have separate conditions.
More scenic and varied than a pure flat-city PR course.
Course
The point-to-point course starts in North Sydney, crosses the Sydney Harbour Bridge, loops through Centennial Park and the Royal Botanic Garden, and finishes at the Sydney Opera House. With 313 metres of climbing, frequent turns, and an 83-metre net descent, it is harder to pace than a flat major.
Race-day weather
Late August in Sydney is usually cool enough for solid marathon racing, though harbour wind and changing sun can still affect effort. It is often friendlier than hot-weather spring races, but the course profile is not as forgiving as Berlin or Chicago.
About 
the TCS Sydney Marathon
Sydney’s marathon crosses the Harbour Bridge and finishes at the Sydney Opera House.

A GPS trace of a recent edition, with elevation, from an open collection of course files, scaled to the certified 42.195 km so the mile markers land where the race's do. The usual rule of thumb at marathon effort: about 12–15 seconds lost per 100 ft of climb and about 8 seconds gained per 100 ft of descent. REGISTRATION CLOSED / SOLD OUT (official organiser notice dated 10 October 2026):
 The organiser confirmed that the 2027 Osaka Half Marathon reached its 7,000-runner capacity and stopped accepting entries on 10 October 2026, ahead of the originally advertised 4 November deadline. The race itself remains scheduled for 31 January 2027. See 
the official news announcement
.
The 2027 Osaka Half Marathon is a major city road race held on the same day as the Osaka International Women's Marathon. The 21.0975 km course starts on Tamatsukuri-suji on the east side of Osaka Castle Park and finishes inside Yanmar Stadium Nagai. The organiser describes the course as flat and fast, and it is certified by the Japan Association of Athletics Federations as well as WA/AIMS. The event has a 7,000-runner field and is run as a serious competitive half marathon rather than a casual fun run.
One of the race's distinctive features is its relationship with the Osaka International Women's Marathon. The two events use substantial sections of the same city-road network in opposite directions, allowing half-marathon runners to see elite women's marathon competitors during the race. The stadium finish at Nagai also places runners in one of Osaka's best-known athletics venues.
The gun is at 12:00 JST and the overall limit is 2 hours 5 minutes from the starting signal. Seven intermediate checkpoints close progressively, beginning at 2.0 km at 12:18 and ending at 20.6 km outside Yanmar Stadium Nagai at 14:05. Runners who miss a checkpoint must stop racing and follow officials' instructions.
Start seeding places invited athletes and recommended Kansai Student Half Marathon Championship runners first, followed by an A block for qualifying runners, then other entrants by predicted finish time. A-block standards are 1:20:00 for men and 1:35:00 for women using eligible half-marathon performances from 1 January 2025 onwards, with proof due by 6 November 2026.
Registration opened on 5 August 2026 but 
closed early on 10 October 2026 when the 7,000-place capacity was reached
; the originally listed 4 November deadline is superseded. Entrants with unpaid registration must follow their original payment deadlines, according to the organiser. Athlete bib collection is available on 30 or 31 January 2027, with exact reception times due in the participant email sent in early January. Runners must collect their own bibs. On race day, baggage can be deposited at Osaka Castle Park and is transported to Nagai Park for collection after finishing. No race-day parking is available at the start or finish, so public transport is required.

- **Mýrdalshlaupið** - 비크에서 매년 5월 말 개최되는 트레일 러닝 대회
  - 21km (고저차 1,100m), 10km (고저차 490m), 3km 코스
  - 2027년 대회: 5월 29일
  - 공식 사이트: [myrdalshlaup.is](https://myrdalshlaup.is/)

## 👥 현지 러닝 크루 모임

비크는 인구 약 300명의 작은 마을이라 현지 러닝 크루가 없습니다. 대신 **레이캬비크**(비크에서 차로 약 2.5시간)의 러닝 크루 정보를 안내드려요:

### 1. Mikkeller Running Club Reykjavík
- **모임 일정**: 매월 첫째 토요일
- **출발 장소**: Session Bar (Bankastræti 14, 101 Reykjavík)
- **특징**: 국제적인 소셜 러닝 클럽. "달리고 맥주 마시기"를 모토로 하는 친목 중심 모임. 초보자 환영
- **Instagram**: [@mrcreykjavik](https://www.instagram.com/mrcreykjavik/)
- **출처**: [NordRun](https://nordrunclubs.com/clubs/mikkeller-running-club-reykjavikreykjavikiceland)

### 2. Reykjavík Runners (Facebook 그룹)
- **특징**: 레이캬비크에 거주하거나 방문하는 러너들을 위한 비공식 그룹 런. 페이스나 경험 무관, 모두 환영
- **Facebook**: [Reykjavík Runners 그룹](https://www.facebook.com/groups/813222338302597/)
- **출처**: Facebook

### 3. City Runners Club Iceland
- **특징**: 아이슬란드 전역의 러닝 트레일과 그룹을 연결하는 커뮤니티. 오전 7시와 오후 5시 30분 정기 모임
- **웹사이트**: [cityrunnersclub.com/en-is](https://www.cityrunnersclub.com/en-is)

**참고사항:**
- 비크는 소규모 마을이라 정기적인 러닝 크루 모임은 없지만, Mýrdalshlaupið 대회 기간에는 많은 러너들이 모입니다.
- 레이니스피아라 검은 모래 해변은 경치가 아름답지만 "스니커 웨이브"(갑자기 밀려오는 큰 파도)가 매우 위험하니 물가에서 달리지 마세요.
- 아이슬란드 날씨는 변덕스러우니 방풍 재킷과 여러 겹 옷을 준비하세요.

여행 시기를 알려주시면 그 달의 평년 날씨 정보도 추가로 찾아드릴게요!

Is it safe to jog on the black sand beaches in Vik?
While the black sand beaches like Reynisfjara are incredibly scenic, jogging directly along the waterline is 
extremely hazardous
 due to unpredictable “sneaker waves” and strong rip currents. It's crucial to stay well back from the water and never turn your back to the ocean. For a safer running experience with stunning views, consider elevated trails such as those near Reynisfjall and Dyrhólaey.
What kind of terrain can I expect on running trails around Vik?
The running trails around Vik offer a diverse landscape shaped by volcanic activity. You'll find coastal paths, dramatic clifftops, and routes with views towards glaciers like Mýrdalsjökull. The terrain can range from gentle gradients on moderate loops to challenging ascents with significant elevation gain on more difficult routes.
Are there any circular running routes available near Vik?
Yes, there are several circular running routes. For example, the 
Hestanesviki loop from Gudvangen
 is a moderate 8.4 km path with gentle gradients, perfect for a scenic run. Another option is the 
Historic Villas on Villa Road – Balestrand loop from Sygna videregående skole
, a 6.0 km trail through varied terrain.
What are some scenic viewpoints or landmarks I can see while jogging in Vik?
Vik offers breathtaking scenery. You can enjoy panoramic views of the black sand beaches, the southern coastline, and the Mýrdalsjökull Glacier from areas like Dyrhólaey. The 
Klukshaug
 viewpoint is also a great spot. The iconic Víkurkirkja church, perched on a hill, provides a picturesque landmark overlooking the village and the black sand beach.
